summary: Investigated 4 schools whose CDS C22 ED applicant/admit counts are blank. Conclusion: all 4 schools intentionally suppress ED-specific statistics in non-CDS channels too. No two-independent-source bar met for any. NYU has one aggregator-derived estimate (~18%) and a single confirmed applicant count (22,000+), but admit count is unpublished — qualifies as REFER, not CLOSED. Other 3 schools have unanimous evidence of non-disclosure across press, school newspapers, and aggregator deep-dives. Recommendation: leave all 4 UNAVAILABLE; optionally promote NYU to REFER with low confidence and explanatory note.

decisions.reason: NYU officially confirms 22,000+ ED applicants for Class of 2028 (NYU press release + Washington Square News) and that 'over half the incoming class' is admitted ED. However, NYU does NOT publish ED admit counts or ED acceptance rate — confirmed across Ivy Coach, College Kickstart, College Transitions, AdmissionSight. Top Tier Admissions states '~18%' ED acceptance rate Class of 2028 but this is a single-aggregator estimate, methodology undisclosed, and conflicts with back-calculation from official figures (5,705 enrolled / ~40-45% yield / over-half ED implies ED admit pool of ~5,700-6,500, suggesting 26-32% ED rate, not 18%). Two-independent-source bar fails: only one number (22,000 applicants) is two-source confirmed. Cannot compute rate without admit count. Recommend remaining UNAVAILABLE; optionally tag as REFER tier with note: 'NYU does not publicly disclose ED admit count; aggregator estimates range 18-32% with no methodological convergence.'

decisions.reason: Tufts has NOT released ED-specific applicant or admit counts for Class of 2028 or 2029. Confirmed across: (1) Tufts Daily's two main admissions articles (Feb 2024 'Class of 2028 first to be admitted post-affirmative action' and April 2024 'Tufts accepts 10% of applicants to Class of 2028') — both mention 'continued increase in ED applicants' but no numbers; (2) Tufts Admissions enrolled-student-profile page — only total apps (33,415) and overall admit rate (10.8%) for Class of 2029, no ED breakdown; (3) Ivy Coach explicitly states 'Tufts University Hasn't Released Recent Data on Early Decision Admission' and CDS 'draws a blank for most recent cycles' — last available data is Class of 2022 (2,262 combined ED applicants, 957 admits, 42.31% — far too stale to attribute to Class of 2028). No public source has ED Class of 2028 applicant or admit counts. Confirmed non-derivable.

decisions.reason: Wake Forest stopped publishing ED admissions statistics in CDS after Class of 2025 — confirmed by Ivy Coach: 'After that, they stopped reporting ED admissions statistics in their Common Data Set.' Last available ED data is Class of 2024 (773 admits / 2,241 applicants = 34.49%) — too stale to attribute to Class of 2028. Old Gold & Black (student newspaper) and news.wfu.edu searches return no ED breakdown for Class of 2028/2029. Wake Forest Facts & Figures page only provides overall data (18,737 apps, 22% admit, 4,066 admits for Class of 2028) without ED split. Confirmed non-derivable.

decisions.reason: Pepperdine has NEVER publicly published ED or EA applicant/admit counts in recent years. Ivy Coach explicitly states: 'Pepperdine hasn't actually published any verifiable acceptance rate data for any of its Early rounds.' For Class of 2029 their table marks all EA and ED I+II rates as 'Not Reported.' Pepperdine offers three early rounds (EA non-binding, ED I and ED II binding) but only provides overall data (11,526 apps, 7,245 admits, ~63% overall for Class of 2028). Seaver College official admissions pages confirm structure but not statistics. One source mentions 'estimated EA acceptance rate of 46.7%' but this is unsourced and methodology undisclosed — single aggregator floor estimate, fails two-source bar. Confirmed non-derivable.
